doc.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012

title: First rehearsal with Thad Jones chart and Kleckley's chord books
summary: Faking Thad Jones's Don't Get Sassy, embarrassed, he was encouraged by Kleckley, who gave him chord books that fixed his reading within months.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: out once.” I did, and it changed my life. Because there were musicians who were all older than me. They were all college and up, and I was 16. And I walked in and I was a self- taught, you know, a piano player. And they threw the first chart in front of me, I remember it was Thad Jones “Don’t Get Sassy.” It had to be 15 pages. Chord symbols. It was a professional level chart. And I looked at it — what’s C sharp plus nine thirteen — what is that? And I had perfect pitch so [scats]. I was through the Milli Vanilli piano for a while, I didn’t know what to play. I was faking it. They were all so good. And oh gosh. It was a blues, so I could hear that much. And then a solo. Now what? So I faked it, and at the end of the day I almost slunk out of there I was so embarrassed. Two hours of this. And these people were so good and I was this kid — what do I have to chase? I wish I had taken those lessons. But the leader, Mark Kleckley, said, “Hey that was terrific. For a first shot out that was great.” And I said, “Aww I disrupted your practice.” And he said, “No come back next week. Here’s a couple of books that might help you.” Books with pictures of hands playing the chords — all 97 chords, every key, every inversion. That’s what that’s called? Oh that’s what an F sharp flat thirteen sharp nine looks like and sounds like. I can do that. And I studied, came back the next week a little bit faster, you know still awful, but within six months just through sheer repetition I got a little bit faster and a little bit — I could have probably read the Tonight Show Band charts because I was doing nothing else.
